trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 2 rows x 5 columns. RECOMPUTED: Delta-total = Delta-sigma + Delta-sigma^{-1} + Delta-avg holds in both rows (7+3+2 = 12 for +proton, 5+5+2 = 12 for +neutron), so the fourth column is exactly the sum of the first three. The fifth column is confirmed against sibling table 1: +18 and +21 per nucleon reproduce all six of that table's shifts via shift = 1 + 18Z + 21N.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: STRUCTURAL NOTE worth flagging to a reader (not an error): the two rows have IDENTICAL Delta-avg (2) and IDENTICAL Delta-total (12) but DIFFERENT Delta-shift (18 vs 21). So Delta-shift is not a function of the four columns that precede it -- the proton/neutron distinction enters only through the sigma vs sigma^{-1} split (7/3 against 5/5), which Delta-total averages away. A reader scanning left to right will expect the last column to be derived from the others and it is not; the parent block should say what supplies the extra 6 and 9.
